item.content:encoded: as another stupid week comes to a close here in America, let’s look back at the dumbest fucking shit that happened.monday: fly the furry skies“many — listen to this — many airline pilots, flight attendants, and air traffic controllers are part of the furry community. lord help us. it’s terrifying, when you think about it.”furries. Tuberville is talking about , the subculture of people who get off on dressing up as animals. according to our hallucinating senator here, there’s an epidemic of cats and dogs piloting aircraft. look, I fly often. I’ve never seen a flight crew dressed up as , have you? of course you haven’t — and neither has Senator You Should Have Worn Your Fucking Helmet, Asshole. but this imaginary issue is what Tommy wants us to be focused on — as if we don’t have enough problems on our plates already.after getting roundly mocked by the entire world for his dumbfuckery, Terminally-Concussed Tommy did what all dipshits do — he doubled down on the dumbfuck.I know the deranged Democrats don’t like the fact that I called out the insane FURRY CULTURE this week. But the truth is, there is an ALARMING number of these DERANGED people working in our airline industry. Don’t believe me? Just a few months ago, PILOTS were MEOWING and BARKING at each other over the radio at DCA.oh my god, these pilots were MEOWING and BARKING. the horror! The audio of pilots meowing and barking at DCA was a longstanding aviation joke/meme on the emergency guard frequency 121.5, unrelated to furries or any subculture, per reports and pilot accounts.. it’s a thing pilots and controllers do to blow off steam, because their jobs are stressful as fuck. this whole ludicrous episode is Peak MAGA. they misunderstand a joke, get all worked up over it for nothing, and then waste everyone’s time by actually standing up in the well of the Senate and expecting us to run around with our hair on fire over bullshit.are there any actual furry pilots? I don’t know. I don’t care. who gives a fuck? all that matters is that we go up in the air, and we come back down safely. beyond that, I don’t give a shit how anyone is dressed, as long as they do their job.no one gives cares, Tuberville. we want healthcare. we want gas that doesn’t cost an arm and a leg. fix that shit. then we can worry about your imaginary problems.maybe our terminally-concussed senator here shouldn’t be flying without a helmet.tuesday: let them eat now here’s Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins with an important message for the American consumer: don’t bother her with your problems. .“if [beef] is too expensive … you can eat chicken, salmon, eggs — there are other great sources of really good protein.”but now that Dear Leader has clownfucked our once-strong economy straight into the shitter, by imposing incoherent tariffs and blundering into an unwinnable don’t-you-dare-call-it-a-war on Iran, the message from the Donnyverse is now go find something else to eat, fuckface.wednesday: try growing a personality, bro “the thing that people miss in modernism, that we take for granted, we have normalcy bias in a certain direction. we consider normal what is actually insane. we consider normal women having unsupervised access to one another — all the time. we consider normal women — like all these things. women having political rule. we consider normal women living unattached from a male, like a husband, like a father, then a husband, for lengthy periods of time. we consider normal — you could fill in the blank with all of these modern feminist outworkings of the original feminist vision.”holy fuck — that’s a lot of words, just to say ‘I’ve never known the touch of a woman.’grow a personality, bro. stop being such a whiny little boy. if you treat women like people, instead of imagining that they’re some subservient species that owes you their attention, you’ll do fine. trust me.thursday: Peak Stupid just got out-peaked “Xi JinPing refused to put his hand over his heart during the US National Anthem just now.”oh my god. the stupid on Laura’s post is about ten feet thick. how can we possibly dig our way out of it?Yes. Because he’s not American.that’s right, President Xi did exactly what he was supposed to do — — because he’s not an American.which brings us quite smoothly to—friday: the further adventures of Some Fucking Idiot™Friday was Day Two of some fucking idiot’s playdate with his despot inamorato, President Xi of China.Trump in 2011: The president of China came a few months ago and we gave him a state dinner. Now, when people are screwing you, you don't give them state dinners.Trump in 2015: I would not be throwing Xi Jinping a dinner. I would get him a McDonald’s hamburger and say ‘we have to get down to work.’ We’re giving him a state dinner and what he has done is sucked all of our jobs.holy shit. how embarrassing.Melania trying to free her hand from Trump's grasp is sad to watch. you can imagine her going, ‘fock you, Donal, I no care eef you fall. maybe diaper norse want to hold you hand.’that shit must be giffed for posterity’s sake.NEW ANGLE: 📸Melania appeared to be giving Donald a piece of her mind after he held her hand not once but twice. 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Trump points toward the media, pauses then becomes animated. Imagine if the beast had media coverage 🤣🤣you sure hate to see such a formerly happy couple going through a bad patch, don’t you?Now that the pool is there, Trump is finally getting questions: “Did you call on President XI to stop buying oil from Iran? Why are you banning media outlets? Should taxpayers pay for ads about you”but even though the press was actually asking some important questions for a change, not one reporter stood up to ask the one question America wants an answer to, ‘what the fuck is wrong with you?’how fucking idiotic was that?and now, let’s put a close to This Week in Stupid and have us some Daily Claudia.today’s let’s have us some random beachy fun. here’s Ms Spouse with some ocean-side dining, from August 24, 2002.here’s Katie and her mom in Newport, Rhode Island, early 1990s.and this last one’s from Plymouth, MA, early 1990s.have a non-stupid Saturday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future:practice self-care. do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Parametrised tests in Rust with named parameters
item.author: Alex Chan
item.content:encoded:
I’ve been revisiting some of my small Rust utilities this week, and I wanted to improve the test suite. There’s a lot of repetition, and I wanted to switch to parametrised tests, a pattern I use a lot in Python and Go. (These are also called “table-driven tests”.)Parameterised tests allow you to write the test logic once, then run it with many different inputs and expected results. This reduces repetition, highlights variation, and simplifies adding new cases.For example, in my thumbnail creator, I want to create a thumbnail with various image formats, and check the thumbnail has the correct filename and dimensions. Rather than copy-pasting test functions, I wanted to declare test cases with named fields, like this: img_path target TargetDimensionMaxWidth expected_filename expected_dimsSupporting this syntax required me to create a custom Rust macro.I found three existing approaches to writing this type of test in Rust:Use a loop over the test cases. This is the simplest approach: define our test cases in an array, then iterate over them one-by-one.#[test] test_cases fibonacciinput expectedThis is easy to write and understand, but Rust’s standard assertions don’t give us test case isolation. If one case fails, the test stops immediately and skips the rest.(Go’s testing library has , which marks a test as failed but allows it to continue running. When a test fails, you often have more information than if the test had failed immediately. I now miss this when working in other languages.)Define a macro with positional arguments. Many guides, such as over-code’s article, define custom macros with positional arguments.fib_testNamed test cases are nice, but positional arguments hurt readability if you have more than a few parameters.
#[rstest] #[case(1, 1)] #[case(6, 8)] #[case(10, 55)] #[case] #[case] expected fibonacciinputIf I was working in a larger codebase, I’d compare these libraries and pick my favourite.I deliberately skipped them this time, because I only use Rust for tiny personal tools, and I write it as a learning exercise. I’d rather write a basic version myself and learn something new, than use somebody else’s library and miss out on the lesson.Since I couldn’t find a macro that gave me named parameters, I decided to write my own.Here’s the complete macro invocation for my image thumbnailer, with three test cases:image_thumbnail_tests img_path target TargetDimensionMaxWidth expected_filename expected_dims img_path target TargetDimensionMaxWidth expected_filename expected_dims img_path target TargetDimensionMaxWidth expected_filename expected_dimsThe goal is to have clear, self-documented test cases. You can see what the test does and how to add a new test case without reading the body of the macro.Here’s the macro definition, with extra whitespace to make the structure more obvious: $( ident img_pathexpr targetexpr expected_filenameexpr expected_dimsexpr $( #[test] PathBuffrom$img_path test_dir create_thumbnailpathout_dir $targetunwrapthumbnail_path out_dirjoin$expected_filenamethumbnail_pathexistsget_dimensionsthumbnail_path $expected_dimsIf we zoom out, the structure of a declarative macro looks like a match expression:I think of the two halves are input/output, but they’re really called matcher/transcriber:The left-hand side (). The matcher defines a pattern of Rust tokens the input code must match precisely, including commas and brackets (but ignoring whitespace). works like a regular expression, matching zero or more instances of the enclosed pattern. and match a Rust identifier and expression, respectively, and bind them to metavariables (similar to named capture groups in regexes).I deliberately designed my pattern to resemble Rust’s struct syntax. Macro inputs don’t have to be valid Rust code, but I wanted something that would look familiar in a Rust file.The right-hand side (). The transcriber is a template for Rust code, which gets substituted in at compile time, replacing metavariables with values captured by the matcher.Here, the iterates over the matches and creates a corresponding function with a attribute. This attribute is why we need to use a macro – there’s no way to dynamically generate new test functions in Rust without macros.When compiled, the macro gets replaced with all the generated code from the transcriber, as if I’d written out the individual tests in full:#[test] PathBuffrom test_dir create_thumbnailpathout_dir TargetDimensionMaxWidthunwrapthumbnail_path out_dirjointhumbnail_pathexistsget_dimensionsthumbnail_path
#[test] PathBuffromThis means all of my test cases run as separate tests, so I get all the benefits of individual test functions without having to copy-paste lots of boilerplate throughout my codebase.I’ve seen custom macros pop up in the few Rust codebases I’ve read, and it feels good to have a better understanding of how they work. I used to copy-paste the same snippets thoughtlessly from project to project, but now I know what the different brackets and asterisks mean. The next time I write a macro or read somebody else’s, I’ll know what’s going on.

item.title: Saturday Night 80s Jam: Wham! – Wake ME Up Before You Go Go
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: Wham!’s “Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go” is one of the most instantly recognizable pop songs of the 1980s, a bright, energetic blast of pure fun that perfectly captured the carefree spirit of the decade. Released in 1984, it became Wham!’s first No. 1 single in both the United States and United Kingdom and turned George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley into international superstars.Written and produced by George Michael, the song was inspired by a note left for him by Andrew Ridgeley. Michael took the unusual phrase “go-go” and transformed it into one of pop music’s most memorable hooks. The recording combines a bouncy rhythm, handclaps, horns, layered backing vocals and Michael’s enthusiastic lead performance.The song’s greatest strength is its sheer sense of joy. There is no complicated message or heavy emotional baggage. It is simply designed to make people smile, dance and sing along. Michael’s vocals are confident and playful, while the production gives the track an almost unstoppable momentum.The accompanying music video was equally important to the song’s identity. Michael and Ridgeley appeared in colorful, deliberately exaggerated 1980s clothing, helping establish the visual style associated with Wham! and the decade itself. The “Choose Life” shirts became particularly memorable pieces of pop culture.“Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go” remains one of the ultimate feel-good records of the 1980s. Its infectious chorus, exuberant production and colorful personality have allowed it to survive decades of changing musical trends. It is impossible to hear those opening sounds without immediately being transported back to peak 1980s pop.

item.title: Protesilaos: Emacs: I am experimenting with a Denote cache
item.author: Protesilaos
item.content:encoded: The goal is to explore what can be done and whether it makes sense to have that as a feature that users can enable, either directly in or as a separate package.For the time being, I have what I call : https://github.com/protesilaos/denote-data. This is not for users and does nothing useful right now. I have not written any documentation on purpose. I am making it available as a proof-of-concept in case there are interested parties who want to contribute to the project.What I have right now seems solid, though I suspect it will only be useful at scale if the caching is done asynchronously. I plan to to read the manual and check functions such as to understand how we can do something in the background without blocking Emacs.If that is done, then the rest is a matter of (i) extending to cover all cases where files need to be indexed and (ii) plugging it into core Denote functions.At any rate, this is an experiment. If it proves useful, then I will do what is necessary to make it work with Denote as an opt-in feature.Denote is a simple note-taking tool for Emacs. It is based on the idea that notes should follow a predictable and descriptive file-naming scheme. The file name must offer a clear indication of what the note is about, without reference to any other metadata. Denote basically streamlines the creation of such files while providing facilities to link between them.Denote’s file-naming scheme is not limited to “notes”. It can be used for all types of file, including those that are not editable in Emacs, such as videos. Naming files in a consistent way makes their filtering and retrieval considerably easier. Denote provides relevant facilities to rename files, regardless of file type.

item.title: Irreal: Quick Look For Emacs
item.author: Irreal
item.content:encoded:
A quick look at a Quick Look for Emacs from Charles Choi. MacOS has the notion of a Quick Look to peek at a file without invoking a heavier weight application such as an editor. It’s more than just dumping text onto the screen. It can deal with text, PDFs, HTML, various video files, ODF, Microsoft file types, and many others.
Choi likes the Quick Look functionality but, of course, would like to have it in Emacs too. It’s not clear how to do this in general but it’s trivially easy to do it for Dired and Ibuffer. Choi solves the problem by binding and ibuffer-visit-buffer-other-window-noselect to the key. These commands open the file in another window so they’re more than just open the file as usual in Emacs.
If you like the idea of being able to peek at a file without abandoning your current window, take a look at Choi’s post for the details on how to do it from Dired and Ibuffer windows.

item.title: Don’t You Just Hate Seeing Aileen Cannon in a Pickle?
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: A Funhouse Mirror of CorruptionLet’s end the week with an intriguing — and even amusing — new development in the bogus investigation out of south Florida into the “grand conspiracy” against Donald Trump.As part of the probe, we learned yesterday, DOJ has subpoenaed a group of current and former FBI agents from the Mar-a-Lago documents investigation to provide grand jury testimony.In a very savvy move, lawyers for the agents went to U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon yesterday asking for clarification about whether their clients can testify about the details of Volume II of Special Counsel Jack Smith’s report, which covers the Mar-a-Lago investigation.Cannon, you’ll recall, has bottled up the release of Volume II for years and enjoined DOJ from discussing its contents with anyone outside of DOJ. Anyone outside of DOJ would presumably include grand jurors and the FBI agents own defense counsel.On its face, the filing is a legitimate effort to protect the FBI agents from jeopardy for either refusing to testify or violating Cannon’s order by testifying (or from having to take the 5th).But it’s really doing a whole lot more work than that.It mainly puts Cannon and DOJ in an awkward spot because they’ve taken the position that even Smith couldn’t even testify to Congress about Volume II. But now going along with Trump’s retributive “investigate the investigators” scheme requires that the FBI agents testify.DOJ has already reversed course and said it’s fine for the agents to testify about it, according to the agents’ lawyers, who include Abbe Lowell, Mark Zaid, and Margaret Donovan. Now we’ll see what Cannon comes up with to wriggle out of this apparent bind.But there are many more layers to it. The filing revealed new information about the status of the “grand conspiracy” probe; it gave the agents a public forum to assert their innocence and the righteousness of the Mar-a-Lago investigation; it lays some groundwork for a future claim of vindictive prosecution if the agents were to ever get charged; and it begins to unspool a counter-narrative for other judges, including the 11th Circuit, where this is all going to land eventually.The FBI agents’ lawyers are basically using the filing to expose the funhouse mirror of misconduct here at every level.That’s the short version. If you want more on this:Meanwhile, a separate long-running effort to force the public release of Volume II has been stalled for months at the 11th Circuit, where oral arguments have been scheduled and then rescheduled a half a dozen times. This week they were tentatively rescheduled yet again, for January.The 2026 Big Lie: Noncitizen VotingIt’s not just the disinformation and the abuse of power in service of delegitimizing elections generally — it’s the , which is intended to subvert this particular election. The Trump administration and its state-level allies are ramping up false claims, announcements, rule changes, and prosecutions in the heat of the stretch run for a reason. It’s a choice:After widely publicizing its claim last month that it had found massive noncitizen voting in Nevada — to the tune of nearly 16,000 noncitizens — DHS whittled down the actual number of suspected noncitizen voters to 185 and sent that list to the state, which has now confirmed that on the list is a U.S. citizen.ICYMI: In an echo of the 2006-07 U.S. attorneys scandal, top Trump DOJ official Aakash Singh warned managers in a recent conference call that federal prosecutors could be fired if they decline to investigate and pursue cases of reported election fraud, MS NOW reported.The State Department is moving to give state and local officials — and potentially some nonprofit organizations — access to passport records to verify voters’ citizenship, Bloomberg reports. It’s not clear which nonprofit groups would have access to passport records.Florida state officials held a press conference yesterday to announce that 20 people have been charged with voting illegally, most of whom are apparently noncitizens who registered to vote.The Corruption: Love Me EditionClaiming it was a public service announcement — not a political ad in the final weeks of the midterms elections — the Trump White House won’t disclose the funding source for a pro-Trump 30-second TV ad that began running on cable news Wednesday night with the label “Paid for by the U.S. Government.”The background music the TV spot is “Love Me” by JMSN, who did not authorize use of the song.“I am looking for a lawyer now in order to see what our options are and how to proceed,” JMSN told Politico. “I have never been in this situation before, so need help in navigating something of this magnitude.”Trump’s Media Ban Lifted … MostlyAfter a chaotic morning yesterday when it appeared the Trump White House was flouting an overnight court order lifting the president’s ban on CNN, Politico, and MS NOW, reporters from the three outlets did eventually get their hard passes back and were allowed to access the White House.However, a boycott of the TV pool by major networks continues until the White House confirms that CNN will be allowed to resume pool duties.In a troubling attack on a free press, the state of Florida and a conservative think tank have filed a shareholder derivative suit against the parent company of the NYT, claiming the board of directors is exercising insufficient oversight of the newsroom leading to anti-Israel bias in the paper’s coverage of the Israel-Hamas war.“Although it is positioned as a corporate governance petition to inspect the company’s books and records, it is a transparent attempt to exert agenda-driven pressure against an independent media organization, level false allegations of bias and chill journalism protected by the First Amendment,” a NYT spokesperson said of the lawsuit in state court in New York.3rd Country Removals Back at SCOTUSThe Trump administration scrambled to halt third-country deportations yesterday after a late night appeals court ruling blocked its brutal policy while it also immediately sought relief from the ruling at the Supreme Court.According to the NYT: “On Thursday, as news of the ruling spread inside the U.S. government, officials quickly moved to take deportees off flights to third countries such as Costa Rica, Honduras, and the Central African Republic, according to documents obtained by The Times.”The Trump DOJ tried to do an end run around Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, who is the circuit justice for the 1st Circuit, which blocked the third-country removal policy. But that effort didn’t seem immediately successful. She didn’t issue the administrative stay the administration sought, and gave lawyers representing the deportees until Monday at 4 p.m. ET to respond to the DOJ filing.In the run-up to the midterm elections, the Trump DOJ is enlisting military attorneys as temporary federal prosecutors in support of immigration enforcement surges in Manhattan, Los Angeles, and Sacramento, according to a Defense Department email reviewed by Bloomberg Law.Trump’s mass deportation operation has taken on a lower profile since the federal occupations of Los Angeles, Chicago, and Minneapolis, but it is no less sweeping. As arrests rose through the summer, the NYT tried to capture the scale of the intrusion:Federal agents appeared in nearly every corner of daily life, carrying out operations at hospitals and airports, outside suburban schools and along rural construction sites and truck stops. They fanned out from coastal cities in Maine to desert towns in Arizona, across the open plains of Wyoming and down through the southern borderlands.Courthouse News Service: In a final ruling against ICE, U.S. District Judge Lewis Kaplan blasted the “dreadful” and “squalid” conditions at 26 Federal Plaza, the controversial immigrant detention center in New York City.Broadview 6 Prosecutor ResignsAhead of a pivotal contempt of court hearing next week, Sheri Mecklenburg, the federal prosecutor at the center of the Broadview 6 scandal, abruptly resigned yesterday while pointing the finger at embattled U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros.Mecklenburg, who said she resigned because the Trump DOJ would not let her file a response in her own defense for the upcoming hearing, promptly submitted a filing in the case claiming she had followed instructions from Boutros and kept him fully apprised of her handling of the case before the grand jury.The federal case against ICE protesters was already shaky but it collapsed and was dismissed after revelations of alleged misconduct in how the case was presented to the grand jury.A Delightful Weekend ReadAlmost anything I say about this piece will be a spoiler, so I’m going to refrain from characterizing it except to say it’s a lovely treatment of a wonderful story with great pacing and a commendable narrative structure. Enjoy!Scientific American: How apple detectives solved the mystery of an ancient tree—and rewrote the history of fruitEnjoy the First Weekend of Fall

item.title: we could all use a Good News Friday
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: spoiler alert: not everything good news is out there — you just have to go looking for it. so today, let’s do exactly that.bear with me, this is another longish post. Good News number one: a lot of this shit has been flying under the radar, but judges and courts continue to cordially invite Donny — along with his like-minded flunkies and acolytes — to go fuck themselves.long story short: back during the 2024 campaign, three days before the election, the Des Moines Register published a poll showing mean old Kamala Harris with a three-point lead over God’s Own Avatar on Earth. of course, that’s not what happened. Donny won Iowa by 18 points — but because Donny is the most-broken-inside piss-baby in the universe, instead of forgetting about the one bad poll and getting on with his infuriatingly charmed life, he went ballistic and sued the paper the pollster, for being .yesterday, an Iowa district court shitcanned the lawsuit, ruling that there’s no First Amendment exclusion for being a dumbfuck who got his feeling hurt by words.the score: justice 1, morons 0.The California Supreme Court on Thursday ordered a county sheriff to return about 650,000 ballots he had seized from election officials as part of an investigation into voter fraud that state officials said had no basis in fact.what we have here is just one more MAGA numb-nuts who was so saddened by an election that didn’t go his way, that he took it upon himself to confiscate a bunch of ballots, this is just one more way in which Donny has broken our nation. now, every dipshit on the losing end of an election believes they have the right to meddle with the results.the California Supreme Court shut that shit down pronto, ruling that after an election isn’t a thing, even if you’re some high-on-your-own-supply cultist with a gun and a badge.the score: justice 2, morons 0.The Trump administration scrambled on Thursday to halt a number of imminent deportations after an appeals court blocked authorities from expelling people to third countries without a chance to contest their cases, according to documents obtained by The New York Times.we’re really on a roll here. the score: justice 3, morons 0.and then we have the whole shittacular farce that played out this week, with Diaper Nurse Natalie sweet-talking Donny into banning CNN, MSNOW and Politico from the White House — which, by the way, is the latest wrinkle in the story: that it was Nurse Natty, taking advantage of Chief of Staff Susie Wiles being away on vacation, who convinced Dear Leader that a media ban would be totes awesome.my god, it’s like a high school lunchroom. there really are no adults at all in the White House.so it was right back to court for everyone involved, where the judge was all, ‘what in the actual fuck?’ and reinstated the reinstated access. double-reinstated, boo-yah!are you all still following me? oh, good. so now, presumably, it will be back to court again this morning.the score: justice 3.5, morons .5.Good News number two: even the loyalists at Fox News seem to finally be getting exasperated with Dear Leader.“those polls showed 51% would vote Democrat, for a Democrat candidate, 43% for a Republican. why is this happening? four dollar gas, six dollar diesel, seven percent mortgages, the ongoing war, and the president is less popular personally than at any time in his second term. his attempts to reverse the trend have fallen flat. five thousand dollar checks for everyone didn’t fly, and the ban on diesel exports won’t work. if this trend continues, Republicans will lose the House, and maybe the Senate. thirty-nine days to the vote. if that happens, say goodbye to what’s left of the Trump agenda.”“say goodbye to what’s left of the Trump agenda”? don’t threaten me with a good time, Stu.after the 2024 election, Republicans had the golden goose: the House, the Senate, the presidency were all theirs, and they could do anything they wanted. Donny took that golden goose and clownfucked it so hard that their agenda currently lies in tatters — and now, far too late to do anything about it, Republicans are waking up to the fact that maybe this guy the answer.look at these two lovebirds. have you ever seen a two people more head-over-heels smitten with each other?seriously, Melly’s in shitfit mode because her whole weekend has been ruined by having to pretend to about the husband whom she loathes, and his playdate with what’s-his-face from . look, it’s enough that Melania deigned to show up. please don’t ask her to bother to learn anyone’s name, or where they’re from.and as for Donny, he just realized that he and his diaper nurse can’t spend the weekend canoodling.Good News number four: Dear Leader can’t stop being a clownshoes buffoon.what can possibly be going on? is he wearing some kind of medical device? has Natalie chosen to make things easier for herself by having Donny wear the diapers at once?There is no factual or medical news regarding Donald Trump’s health or physical condition concerning his lower back or posture.you’re no fun, plagiarism robot — but you do get bonus points for knowing who I was referring to when I said Good News number five: Dear Leader continues to deteriorate, both physically and mentally.yesterday, Donny had exactly : to walk in a straight line for six feet, without fucking that shit up. Donny can’t even manage to walk on his side of the red carpet. he keeps meandering to his left, forcing his Slovenian rent-a-wife to walk on the bare concrete of the Epstein Parking Lot where the Rose Garden used to be.was it Donny’s frontotemporal dementia that caused him to veer? or was he deliberately being a dick to Melania, just because he could?who cares? either way, that shit’sand, finally, Good News number six: someday this war’s gonna end.today marks 38 days to the midterm elections. should things go our way, we’re going to have a ginormous fucking mess to clean up.there’s no doubt in my mind that useless pantloads like Chuck Schumer will continue to waste everyone’s time on a series of strongly-worded letters — but at the same time, folks on our side who are right now giving serious thought as to what we’ll need to do, in order to dig out from under this shitpile Donny’s inflicted on us.10 Steps To Fix What Trump Has BrokenAnd mend everything thereafterIf we want to clean up the mayhem Trump and his regime have created — and prevent anything like this from happening again — here are the 10 big reforms every political candidate should support.They’re structural reforms in how our political system works, rather than policies such as Medicare for All, affordable housing, childcare, or a $20 minimum wage. But these structural reforms are necessary prerequisites to getting good policies enacted. They must be passed by Congress in order for anything else to get done.I’m summarizing them below the video. Please watch and share:we have our marching orders.well, it’s Friday — and we made it through another week in one piece. let’s reward ourselves with some Daily Claudia and get out of here.I’m pretty sure I’ve posted this triptych before, but since today is the one-year anniversary of this beautiful early-autumn day lunch at 3 Westerly Bar & Grill in Ossining on September 25, 2025, I’m reposting it. have a great Friday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Patrick Cowley
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: It’s Friday so we’re listening to something more upbeat. Today we’re listening to Patrick Cowley, an American electronic musician from Buffalo, NY. Born in 1950, he grew up playing the drums in local bands and then moved to San Francisco when he was 21.He was fascinated by newfangled machines called synthesizers and in the City College learned to play Moogs and Buchlas. At clubs and bathhouses he heard Donna Summer, Giorgio Moroder, Kraftwerk, Tangerine Dream, andmore. Across the ‘70s he developed his own style of synth-driven dance music, collaborating with the singer Sylvester on several hits. We’re playing two of Cowley’s solo records, which were released after he passed away of AIDS-related illness in 1982. from 2017 collects instrumentals he recorded between 1979 and 1982 primarily for adult film soundtracks. , just released last year, collects ten tracks which in the words of the label are “sultry, psychedelic, sarcastic, and just a bit sleazy.”Have a wonderful weekend.

item.title: White House Defies Court Order Lifting Its Media Ban
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: Reporters Rebuffed at White House GatesThe White House immediately defied an overnight court order lifting President Trump’s purported ban on three news outlets from covering the White House.Instead of complying with the court order, this is what happened, according to this morning’s filing by CNN, MSNow, and Politico:The White House turned away journalists from all three news outlets.A Secret Service agent confiscated the hard passes of journalists from all three organizations.When CNN’s Betsy Klein, whose hard pass was previously confiscated on Sept. 19, requested to have her hard pass returned, her request was denied and she was refused access to the White House complex.The Trump DOJ did not respond immediately to inquiries from counsel representing the three news outlets, they said in the filing. They asked the judge to hold teleconference or video conference this morning.Kelly, a Trump appointee, has given the administration until 12:30 ET to respond.Trump Admin Defies Another Court OrderDespite a 1st Circuit Court of Appeals ruling Friday blocking its policy of third-country removals, the Trump administration was pressing ahead yesterday with additional removals, according to a news report and court filings.In the case of a Peruvian man it wants to deport to the Central African Republic, the Trump DOJ argued that the appeals court ruling wasn’t in effect yet, the American Prospect reported.The Trump DOJ reiterated that position in a phone call with lawyers who had brought the 1st Circuit case, and late last night they filed an emergency request for the appeals court to issue its mandate, which would remove any doubt — if there was any — about its ruling being in effect.The lawyers, who cited the American Prospect’s reporting in their filing, told the appeals court: “Class counsel has learned from multiple sources that a flight holding class members is scheduled to depart tomorrow from Alexandria, Louisianna (sic) with identified destinations as Burundi, Rwanda, and Central African Republic.”In response, the 1st Circuit issued an order just before midnight dissolving the stay of a lower court order that had blocked the policy — with the effect of making its ruling operative now.In this very same case, when it was at the lower court in Boston in March 2025, the Trump administration engaged in repeated flagrant violations of court orders by continuing with third-country removals.The American Prospect’s Gillian Brockell, who has been doing exemplary work on third-country removals, has been tracking the latest developments since just before midnight, including flights en route to African countries:Cuban Wins Release in 3rd Country CaseA federal judge in Brownsville ordered the release of a Cuban tow truck driver from Miami who has lived in the United States for 30 years and who the Trump administration has tried to deport to Mexico at least three different times over the past 15 months.Reinaldo Moreno-Rodriguez, who has been in ICE custody since June 2025, outlined his harrowing experience in an affidavit in a separate case. He alleges that he was beaten by guards at ICE’s Camp East Montana after he initially refused to get on a bus apparently bound for Mexico.By his account, Moreno-Rodriguez was taken as far as a border crossing with Mexico and ordered to walk to a waiting bus on the Mexican side. After he began yelling in protest that he was being kidnapped, the Mexican guard refused to accept him, he recounted in the affidavit:The judge ruled that Moreno-Rodriguez’s continued detention after 15 months in custody is unlawful because “there is currently no plan for Petitioner’s removal—let alone a plan that would secure his removal in the reasonably foreseeable future.” He ordered Moreno-Rodriguez’s release on or before Sept. 26.New Details on ICE Stop of US CitizenThe NYT has published new video of and interviewed witnesses to ICE agents accosting a U.S. citizen Sunday in Evanston, Illinois. The man suffered injuries to his head, neck, and teeth before the ICE agents left him lying in the street. Local police are investigating the incident.Four newly revealed incidents show that OpenAI agents were engaged in rogue behavior even before the Hugging Face hack. The hacks in May and June involved:a digital library at the University of New Mexico;Data USA, a repository of public data about American employment and education;Australia’s Medicare Statistics Reporting Service;the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare.Trump Lawsuit Over Poll Tossed OutA state judge in Iowa threw out President Trump’s lawsuit against the Des Moines Register, its parent company, and longtime pollster Ann Selzer for having published a poll in the stretch run of the 2024 election that showed him losing badly in the state. Trump ended up winning Iowa handily. Trump claimed the poll was a defective product and sued under the Iowa Consumer Fraud Act. No dice, the judge ruled.

item.title: Irreal: Confirm-kill-emacs
item.author: Irreal
item.content:encoded:
00-11 notes that Danrobi1 is misunderstanding the purpose of the variable: it was never about whether to call or to ask if quitting Emacs is really what you want. What its purpose is and was is to specify a predicate that will decide whether to quit Emacs or not. There’s no reason it even has to communicate with the user. It just has to decide whether to quit or not based on whatever logic is coded into it.
I’ve had it set to for as long as I can remember and haven’t thought about it in all that time. But 00-11’s response got me thinking. I originally set it to because I kept inadvertently quitting Emacs by fat fingering some other shortcut and I’ve never looked back but there is one problem.
If I don’t remember to quit Emacs before rebooting my MacBook Pro, the reboot will hang waiting for Emacs to quit. That usually happens when there’s an OS update that I start off when I go to bed expecting to have a new OS in the morning only to find the system still waiting for Emacs to quit.
What if I could detect if my Mac is being rebooted? If I can, I can easily code up a predicate function that quits Emacs if so and calls if not. The thought just popped into my mind so I haven’t had a chance to research it yet but it seems promising.

Donny’s best okay, Big Wheel of Moron™, get us out of here. what else ya got?listen to that. no one has any fucking clue what Donny might be gibbering about, because the static is drowning him out. you know what? I-can’t-hear-a-word-he’s-saying Donny just be my new favorite Donny. this is the kind of rinky-dink Amateur Hour shit that goes on when the grown-ups aren’t around to supervise. this is what Melania is talking about when she says that Dear Leader is doing ‘the best he can.’let’s just throw our heads back in laughter, and give another tug on the Big Wheel.did you know that the White House has been making an entire list of other Emotional Support Buildings that our Attention-Hog-in-Chief can put his accursed name all over? stop smirking, it’s true. MS-NOW aired a whole thing on it last night — and you’ll never guess which historic site is included on that list.wait, what? Ford’s Theatre?honestly, who in the White House thought this was a good idea, to slap the Donny’s name all over where got sic semper tyrannis’d right in the skull? is that really what these dumbfucks want Dear Leader’s name associated with?good lord, they’re all just like their boss, in that they act first and think never — and speaking of their boss, when he heard the news, he threw a thermonuclear hissy.Donny’s childish meltdown — and angry denial — is all the proof you need that this story is one hundred percent true.meanwhile, let’s go live to Melania, for her reaction to the news that Donny’s name might be going up on Ford’s Theatre.go easy on the sauce, Mel — remember, you’re got a whole state dinner to plan.okay, let’s give that Big Wheel one final spin.hey, remember a few months ago, when Donny made that big prime-time speech about how China stole the 2020 election for Sleepy Joe Biden, and even the loyalists at Fox News were all, ‘shut the fuck up, bro, we have real things to worry about’?what ever happened with that?I met President Xi at the plane (Airport!) yesterday and he looks strong, vibrant, and fit - Better than ever. Madam Xi, of course, BEAUTIFUL! President DJTthat’s way too much information, my dude. no one needs to know how much you’re drooling over Xi’s big strong looks, with vibrancy like few thought possible.oh, and thanks for clarifying that wholething, honcho. a lot of us were confused about where one goes to meet planes.but seriously, why is Donny being such an obsequious dipshit for the president of China? the only other person for whom he rolls out the literal red carpet and goes out to meet is his other despot bestie, Putin. our actual allies get treated like crap. Donny waits for them back at the White House, and then tries to pull that infantile Alpha-Top-Dog-Dick-Measuring handshake.he never attempts that shit with Xi or Putin. he’s too sickeningly love-smitten.but here’s my real question: what the fuck was going on with Donny during the military flyover that he’d arranged in honor of his bestie?we really need to gif that shit for posterity’s sake.look at Donny. he’s in actual, serious pain as the flyover occurs, while Xi just stands there like it’s no biggie. nobody else flinches — just Donny.. [1, 2]Why Noise Sensitivity Happens in Dementia [1, 2, 3]oh, huh. tell me, it a bad thing when a country’s chief executive is so impaired that his cognitively-collapsed brain becomes overwhelmed ?you know, maybe someone might ought to have that checked out.hey, guess what: it’s time for our Daily Claudia.here’s a triptych from a three-days-before-her-actual-74th-birthday lunch at Blu Pointe in Newburgh, on February 2, 2024.have a great Thursday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: James Dyer: Copy Only What You See: Teaching M-w a Prefix Argument
item.author: James Dyer
item.content:encoded:
Select a region in a folded Org buffer, press , and you get more than you bargained for: the kill ring receives the hidden text as well. Folding is only a display trick - the text is still in the buffer, and dutifully copies every character between the region boundaries, ellipsis and all. Paste that into an email or a chat and the hidden notes come along for the ride.
The fix, in my config, is a prefix argument: copies only the visible text of the region, leaving everything folded or hidden behind. Plain is unchanged.
I have been a fan of ever since I discovered it works outside Org - back in 2023 I was using it in with to copy just the filenames. The only friction was having to remember instead of my muscle-memory . So I taught my existing wrapper a another trick: hand it a prefix argument and it copies only the visible text. has been remapped to a small wrapper for a while, mainly so that pressing it with no active region copies the current line. The new version forwards the prefix argument into a second branch: ( (beg end copy-visible)
( ( (use-region-p) (list (region-beginning) (region-end) current-prefix-arg) (list (line-beginning-position) (line-beginning-position 2) current-prefix-arg))) ( copy-visible (org-copy-visible beg end) (kill-ring-save beg end))) (global-set-key [remap kill-ring-save] 'my/kill-ring-save) keeps working everywhere.
So why org-copy-visible?, I could have written my own invisible-text walker, but already is one and it ships with Emacs!

item.title: Egberto Gismonti
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today we’re listening to Egberto Gismonti, a Brazilian composer, guitarist, and pianist from Carmo. Born in 1947, he started studying piano at age six, going on to study at in Paris, where he was drawn especially to Ravel’s voicings. Returning to Brazil,he incorporated choro, a fast-paced and expressive traditional Brazilian style into his work. That meant learning the guitar, and amazingly he became virtuosic at a second instrument. In the 1970s he signed with ECM, the German jazz label, which went on to release about a dozen of his records. from 1979 is, as the title suggests, a collection of solo performances on guitar and piano. from 1986 is a collection of energetic piano performances, showcasing his signature blend of classical rigor and folk expression.
